notes:
Three bullets, three rungs, the same shape as its predecessor Hypnotic Hospitality. Bullet 2 is not a step -- it is the shopping list, with a sub-bullet per item saying where that item comes from -- so the fetching is split out ahead of the trade as an obtain, because holding all three at once is the only observable thing this quest offers. The three Mog Garden facilities the page names (Coastal Fishing Net, Pond Dredger, Mineral Vein) all resolve as real entities, but every one of them is offered with an off-Garden alternative on the same line: the Repeat Login Campaign for the calamary, the Auction House for the comet and for the stone. So no single object is the target of the obtain and no single zone is right for it, and it deliberately carries neither -- unlike Hypnotic Hospitality, where the Garden was at least mostly true.

Bullet 1's real gate is Rank 7 in every geological section of the Garden -- the MHMU treatise bought for every section except monster rearing -- which nothing in the packets reports. Fame 'Other' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing, so only the raw survives. The Straw Hat is the reward and so is not evidence. The page gives no grid ref anywhere in the Mog Garden.

steps.note: you must already hold Rank 7 in every geological section of the Garden -- the MHMU treatise bought for all of them except monster rearing -- and then zone in. Neither the rank nor the zoning is observable.

Drill Calamary from the Coastal Fishing Net or the Repeat Login Campaign, Calico Comet from the Pond Dredger or the Auction House (Fish), Philosopher's Stone from the Mineral Vein or the Auction House (Alchemy). Every source has an off-Garden alternative, so this step has no target and no zone.

Bullets 2, 3 and 4 are all Shantotto and are ONE rung: speak to her, zone out and back, speak again, and answer her two questions (either answer to the first, 'No way! Not on your life!' -- the top option -- to the second). Three rungs on one NPC with an unmarkable zone-out wedged between them buys nothing, and the sub-bullet's title change is an outcome, not a step.

Bullet 5 is the shopping list, but its sub-bullet is a real step and the only evidence this quest offers: Hiwon's Hair exists only if you go back and speak to Hiwon-Biwon, and it resolves as an ITEM (552), not a key item, despite reading like one. It is evidence on that step and a requirement on the trade, which is the correct split.

The header puts Shantotto at (K-7); the walkthrough puts her at (K-8), the same square it gives Hiwon-Biwon, which looks like a copy of the line above it. Both are kept where each was written rather than reconciled -- the header's in start.grid, the walkthrough's on the steps.

VERIFY (stage D): demoted to medium. The header names Shantotto as the giver at (K-7), but bullet 1 sends you to a different NPC, Hiwon-Biwon, before her. Either speaking to Hiwon-Biwon is a precondition that has to happen before Shantotto will offer the quest -- in which case rung 1 is not a ladder position at all -- or the walkthrough's ordering is simply loose. notes:
Two bullets and two rungs; everything difficult about this page is in the gates, which is why it is medium rather than high.

'Previous' lists eight quests under 'Any one of the following' -- the eight level-75 limit break quests. prev is an AND-list downstream (any member reading false greys the marker out), so recording all eight would tell every player who did exactly one of them, which is all of them, that they are blocked. prev is therefore left EMPTY and the branch is recorded here instead: Shattering Stars, The Beast Within, Breaking the Bonds of Fate, Achieving True Power, A Furious Finale, Survival of the Wisest, Endeavoring to Awaken, Elementary, My Dear Sylvie. Any one of those opens this quest.

'Quest Reqs: Level 75' is the Level field restated -- any job -- so jobs stays empty and only the level gate is set. The three merit points are a real requirement with no observable predicate; nothing in the packets reports merits, so the trade step carries only the five Kindred's Seals and the merits are a note.

'Nomad Moogle' is one of the resolver's ambiguous names -- there is one in most cities -- which is safe here only because both steps carry Ru'Lude Gardens; a zone-less rung on that name would match every moogle in Vana'diel. The After the walkthrough section is Notes, not steps: seals from a Greeter Moogle for 5 Login Campaign points each, or from Shemo at 3 of any other seal to 1.

steps.note: an ambiguous name that is only safe because the zone is carried with it
you must also be holding 3 unspent merit points, which nothing in the packets reports, so only the seals are recorded. The reward is the level cap itself, not an item.

The page places them only in prose -- 'just south of Hakkuru-Rinkuru on the stage', 'against the wall to the west', 'against the wall to the northeast' -- and gives no grid for any of them, so their grids are null and the positions are notes. (E-7) is Hakkuru-Rinkuru's own square and is not borrowed for them.

Bullet 3 is the shopping and is split out as an obtain, so that holding all three wands is a rung of its own: it is the only observable thing here. The page names no vendor and no place for the Sparks purchase, only the two Sparks tiers, so that step carries no zone. Bullet 4's sub-bullet is an outcome -- two of the three items come back at the end of the cutscene -- which is also the reason none of them could ever be evidence that the quest is finished. 'Quest Reqs: Mythril Rod, Rose Wand, Oak Staff' is the item list restated, not a gate.

notes:
Seven bullets, eight rungs, and two of the splits are the whole point of reading this page rather than scanning it.

Bullet 1 both starts the quest and says where the Cathedral Tapestry comes from, so the drop becomes its own obtain step: it carries Orcish Fighter as a drop mob but NO zone, because the page offers Fort Ghelsba or the Yughott Grotto and a step may only have one zone. Splitting it into two rungs would invent a sequence the player does not have to follow.

Bullet 4's sub-bullets are the opposite trap. Buds Bunny, Swagger Spruce and Targe Beetle are named only to reassure you that they do NOT aggro -- they are bystanders, not droppers -- so no mob is recorded against the Ordelle Chest Key; the page says only 'certain monsters in the cave'. A verb-and-name scanner would have made them the target of that step.

Bullet 5's chest is never named ('a chest inside'), so nothing is invented: the step keeps its zone, its key requirement and its key item, and simply has no target. Both key steps are properly evidenced and neither shares evidence: the Ordelle Chest Key at the step that farms it, the Torn-out pages at the step that opens the chest.

Bullets 6 and 7 are two different NPCs in two different zones and stay separate rungs.

Three bullets, three rungs, and the decision that matters is what NOT to record. The page says to defeat three Numbing Blossoms and that 'you obtain the required items automatically', but it never names that item, Item Reqs is empty, and 'Numbing Blossom' resolves ONLY as a monster -- neither as an item nor as a key item. So the fight step carries the mob with a count of three and no evidence at all, rather than minting an item name out of the monster's. Nothing in this quest is observable; the ladder rests on the session latch alone, which is the honest answer for a three-rung kill-and-return.

Bullet 1's sub-bullet and the whole After the walkthrough Notes section say the same thing twice -- you must zone after Dirt Cheap to FLAG this quest, but not to repeat it -- which is a precondition and not a step. The page gives no grid anywhere: Mano-Amano is at the Frontier Station, and the two hunting spots are described only in prose. Fame 'Seekers of Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

notes:
The header's giver is not the giver. It names Amchuchu, but no bullet on this page ever talks to her -- every interaction with her is 'Check Amchuchu's Laboratory', which resolves as a real, targetable entity in its own right at (J-10). Start is moved there and the header string is kept verbatim in start.raw: that is a marker MOVE, not a removal, the same shape as the House of the Hero in the Summoner quests.

Bullet 1 is a precondition -- one in-game day after Vegetable Vegetable Evolution -- and folds into step 1's note. The conditional wait inside bullet 3 (if Chanteillie does not say Amchuchu is ready, wait a game day after trading and come back) folds into that step's note rather than becoming a wait rung, because the rung after it is already a real markable object and a wait rung would only push the mark off it. Neither game-day wait is observable.

Amchuchu's Missive is a key item (2505), granted at bullet 4, so that is the step that carries it and the only evidence this quest offers. Bullets 2, 4 and 6 are three separate visits to the same Laboratory with a trade and a trip to Bastok between them, so they are three rungs and not one -- this is the case the 'unless the page really does' clause exists for. Chanteillie has no square of her own on the page; she is at the Inventors' Coalition, the same building as the Laboratory. The trailing 'Note:' about Raptor Rapture is already covered by Previous. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions.

notes:
Five bullets, six rungs, because bullet 4 is two things: farming a Shell Bug off a Brass Quadav, and trading it to Nichais. The farm has no place -- 'in present-era Vana'diel' is the whole point of that sentence, since this is a Wings of the Goddess quest and the Quadavs are on the far side of the era line from everything else here -- and the page names no zone for it, so that step carries the mob and the item and no zone at all.

Bullet 1's sub-bullet is a dialogue choice: 'Immensely, yes' continues, 'Not in the least, no' only makes you leave and start the scene again. It is not a rung. Bullets 2 and 5 are the same Timeworn Altar at the same square, and they stay two rungs because the page really does put a return to Nichais and an item hunt between them.

Like Operation Teatime, this quest ENDS away from any NPC: bullet 5's altar gives the final cutscene and the two random jewels, and no hand-in on Nichais is invented. The wiki's '(S)' zone names resolve exactly as written, so they are kept in the wiki's form. Fame 'Wings of the Goddess' is an expansion name, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing.
